sample_student_quotes: A class and an object are basically the same thing in memory; declaring class Car creates the car in the heap.
Writing class Dog creates an actual Dog object in RAM immediately when the code runs.
CLASS_IS_AN_OBJECT.remediation_suggestion:
Pedagogical Intervention:
  Writing class Dog defines what a Dog looks like. No Dog exists in memory until you write new Dog(). How many Dogs exist after class Dog alone? Zero.
Key Takeaway: A class occupies no runtime memory for instances until instantiated.
